sections.content: How many people stayed in Newport (Isle of Wight) after gaining qualifications?

Newport (Isle of Wight) is a medium-sized town in the South East. Newport (Isle of Wight) does not have its own university.

Newport (Isle of Wight) has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Newport (Isle of Wight) ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,180 state-school pupils from Newport (Isle of Wight) who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 265 (22%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 395 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Newport (Isle of Wight) to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Newport (Isle of Wight)'s pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Newport (Isle of Wight) in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Newport (Isle of Wight) move to?

Of Newport (Isle of Wight)'s graduates, 130 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those graduates (19%) were living fairly locally, in the Isle of Wight travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Newport (Isle of Wight)'s qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 140 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those qualified non-graduates (57%) were living fairly locally, in the Isle of Wight travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Newport (Isle of Wight)'s GCSE cohort:

  • 65 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was the South West
  • 35 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 34% of graduates and 40% of qualified non-graduates living in Newport (Isle of Wight) had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 205 graduates and 405 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Newport (Isle of Wight). This is compared with the 265 graduates and 395 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 63% of the graduates had also lived in Newport (Isle of Wight) as GCSE pupils, while 34% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Newport (Isle of Wight) in 2018 to 2019, 62% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 40% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
